newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-EUROPEAN PRIZE FOR FRENCH LEAGUE CUP VICTORS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EUROPEAN PRIZE FOR FRENCH LEAGUE CUP VICTORS.

text.p: Bordeaux and Strasbourg hope that their clash in the French League Cup final on Saturday will be the start of a new era and offer them a place in Europe next season.
Both sides have prestigious histories but both have struggled in recent seasons to make it back to the top.
Strasbourg have not won a major honour since their last league title in 1979 and few fans remember that they won the inaugural League Cup held in 1963 and given up the following season.
Bordeaux have lifted no trophy since their 1987 French league and cup double.
The League Cup was resurrected three years ago, with Paris St Germain and Metz each winning once since its return.
A ticket for next season's UEFA Cup is at stake, with neither club yet certain of a place in Europe on the strength of league position.

Bordeaux seem to have more to lose. They are sixth in the first division table, two points behind Strasbourg, and have been beaten by Montpellier in their last two outings in the French Cup and the league.
The Bordeaux squad looks tired and reports say coach Rolland Courbis may be on his way to Marseille, Japan or an Italian club at the end of the season.
"If we could play our last six league matches knowing we've won the League Cup, the atmosphere would be very different," Courbis said.
But Strasbourg, who lost the last final they played in the 1995 French Cup against Paris St Germain, are in a similar position.
"Two years ago we took the Cup final as a reward in itself. Against Bordeaux we must look for victory. Defeat would be a big disappointment," coach Jacky Dugueperoux said.

Strasbourg's morale may be boosted by the fact that they won away to Bordeaux in the league and drew at home but they are likely to be without solid goalkeeper Alexander Vencel of Slovakia, who twisted an ankle in training.
He should be replaced by young David Klein, who has played only two first division matches.
